frame_scale_note: PIA00453 panels are blown up x1.75 relative to native NAC pixels (measured on the Earth panel, +-15%; assumed for all six). NAC: 0.424 deg over 800 px (NAIF vg1_issna_v02.ti).
roll_note: No scan-platform pointing survives for 1990 (PDS VGISS ends 1989-09-29; NAIF CK is bus-only). Earth: Sun-derived as in pbd.json. Venus: same twist as Earth (PIA00450 shows both insets with identical orientation). Jupiter-Neptune: twist relative to Earth taken from the tilts of their wide-angle frames in the PIA00451 mosaic (mod 90, smallest turn, +-5 deg). Every frame inherits the Earth frame's 180-deg sign question: alt_sun_toward_top flips them all. The outer planets are point sources, so their roll barely shows.

not_imaged.Mercury: too close to the Sun (0.39 deg from it as seen from Voyager 1)
not_imaged.Mars: not detectable because of scattered sunlight in the optics (1.26 deg from the Sun)
not_imaged.Pluto: too small and too far from the Sun (too dim)

mosaic.projection: gnomonic (flat plane): the image is a rectangle on the plane tangent to plane_normal_dir at unit distance; place corners at v1 + D*corner
mosaic.fit_points_note: label-glyph centroids (J, E, V, S, U, N and the Sun) in the 4000x1200 NASA original; the saved JPEG is x0.75
mosaic.note: Hand-assembled MIPL mosaic of wide-angle frames spanning ~55 deg; it is not a rigorous projection. Flat-plane fit with free tangent point: see fit_rms_deg. Good enough to hang as a backdrop card behind the planet frames at ~1-2 deg accuracy; the inset thumbnails (JUPITER, EARTH...) around its edge are NOT at their sky positions.

mesh.note: Rows top->bottom, columns left->right, uv = (col/(nx-1), 1-row/(ny-1)). Each vertex is a unit sky direction from Voyager 1 (place at v1 + D*dir). Stereographic fit plus a thin-plate correction so each planet letter lands on its planet; between letters it is an interpolation of a hand-assembled mosaic (~1 deg). NASA's labeled inset thumbnails are blanked in the -clean image.

sun_earth_venus.projection: gnomonic (flat plane): the image is a rectangle on the plane tangent to plane_normal_dir at unit distance; place corners at v1 + D*corner
sun_earth_venus.fit_points_note: pixel coords are in the 3430x2650 NASA original; the saved JPEG is x0.5
sun_earth_venus.note: WA Sun frame (methane filter, 0.005 s) with the Earth and Venus NAC colour frames inset at the WA scale. Placement fits the ephemeris to <0.1% in scale and ~0.2 deg in angle with only 3 points (Sun, Earth, Venus), so it is a precise panel. Its insets are the PBD rotated 90 deg clockwise, which puts the Sun toward the PBD's TOP (the alt_sun_toward_top roll), opposite to NASA's 2020 caption.
